task.title: Money Flow Wedge Scout
task.objective: Discover the strongest tiny programmable software/AI intervention inside an existing large private-sector money flow, continuously rank a best surviving hypothesis, attack it when all build gates appear satisfied, and persist every run so future runs continue from accumulated evidence rather than restarting.

operating_protocol.discovery_floor: Every run must return at least one best surviving hypothesis, even if some gates remain uncertain.
freeze_build_threshold: recurring measurable leakage or unrealized value
credible tiny fee stronger than obvious self-serve or flat-fee alternatives
no need to own the core transaction or request path
no dominant or sufficiently close incumbent or first-party feature
operating_protocol.search_behavior: Before threshold maintain a current leader and try to beat it. At threshold enter ATTACK and search for disconfirming evidence. If it survives, freeze and build; if it fails, record fatal flaw and promote the next candidate.
operating_protocol.persistence_rule: Every scheduled or manual run must append its normalized result, candidate scores, gate changes, evidence, rejected reasons, current leader and next research test to Taskman persistence before the run is considered complete.

conversation_history.summary: Opportunity search narrowed away from tenders, jobs, freelance lead hunting, buyer/seller matchmaking, manufacturer sourcing and generic demand creation toward programmable interventions in existing private money flows.
Adopted eight strict build gates and lifecycle SEARCH -> ATTACK -> FROZEN-BUILD.
Rejected after attack because trigger was customer-created, intervention sat on the request path, first-party cheaper lanes and gateways existed, and performance pricing was weak.
Added two-level standard: every run must return a best surviving hypothesis while final build threshold stays strict; search breadth widened and now drills flow -> state transition -> micro-decision.
Clean authorization/fulfillment/expiry trigger, later weakened by first-party capture/reauthorization features and payment orchestration.
Strong minimum-spend shortfall economics, later weakened by cloud commitment managers and procurement/SaaS allocation tooling.
Excellent economics but current systems reconcile volume commitments, deficiency payments and make-up rights.
Promising pattern: two legitimate future uses already exist and a contractual or quota state changes which is economically optimal; detect before the decision and redirect existing activity.
Prepaid messaging credits plus scheduled sends created a good trigger; later search found mature multi-provider SMS routing/cost optimization layers, increasing feature-absorption risk.
GitHub/Taskman selected as permanent anchor for search state, evidence, rejected paths, scores, task results and conversation-derived knowledge.
Every recurring research run must read Taskman first and persist the full normalized result back to Taskman before completion.

Included/prepaid SaaS or API capacity approaches reset while already-planned deferrable workloads exist and overage/PAYG cost is avoidable. Buyer-side timing/allocation around the billing boundary appears less directly served than seller-side billing, data-enrichment waterfall routing, or messaging orchestration.

current_leader.name: Quota-boundary workload timing optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: included/prepaid usage quota exists -> real system exposes remaining quota and reset/billing boundary -> already-planned non-urgent workload exists -> continuing now would create overage or leave other paid capacity unused -> schedule/allocate eligible work across the boundary -> avoid incremental spend while consuming already-paid capacity
current_leader.why_survived: The quota/reset event is independently machine-readable; many APIs expose remaining quota and reset timestamps; the intervention can begin as a read-only recommendation against existing job queues; the financial delta can be computed as avoided overage/PAYG minus any execution cost; current search found many seller-side metering/billing products but no dominant buyer-side cross-SaaS workload timing optimizer for arbitrary quotas.
strongest_evidence: Multiple current SaaS/API products expose quota remaining and reset dates or explicitly state that unused credits reset/expire each billing cycle.
Apollo credits expire at the end of the billing cycle; Coresignal and other data APIs use recurring credit pools; several APIs expose usage endpoints or quota headers.
Usage-based SaaS billing products confirm that allowances plus overages are widespread, making the boundary economically meaningful.
current_leader.closest_threat: A broad SaaS spend-management platform or provider-native workload scheduler could add buyer-side quota-aware timing. Narrow verticals such as data enrichment already have waterfall routers, so the wedge must avoid categories where routing itself is mature.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read quota/balance/reset data plus an existing job queue or batch schedule; classify jobs by deadline and provider/capability eligibility; recommend RUN-NOW, DEFER-UNTIL-RESET, or USE-ALREADY-PAID-CAPACITY. Do not proxy requests initially.
current_leader.monetization: Per verified boundary-saving event or a small percentage of objectively avoided overage/PAYG spend; if percentage pricing is weak, charge a small fee only when a recommendation produces a measured avoided charge.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: The exact annual buyer-side leakage pool is not yet quantified, and arbitrary cross-SaaS workload interchangeability may be too heterogeneous. If most useful workloads cannot be delayed or reassigned without sitting on the request path, the candidate fails structurally.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find one high-volume non-AI, non-data-enrichment SaaS/API family where (a) included quota expires/resets, (b) overage or alternative PAYG spend is material, (c) queued work has machine-readable deadlines, and (d) no existing product performs buyer-side quota-boundary scheduling. Quantify real avoided dollars per account and test whether read-only recommendations are enough to capture value.

rejections_or_failed_attacks.reason: Apollo and other waterfall enrichment systems already connect multiple providers, meter per-source credit usage and route requests; exact vertical is too occupied.

Shopify now provides automatic capture per fulfillment for Plus and a current Shopify app automatically captures shipped amounts across split fulfillments; Stripe and Adyen expose mature multicapture semantics. Gate 8 is too threatened.

runner_ups.reason: Expiry remains real, but current multi-provider SMS orchestration layers already optimize cost, reliability and routing across existing provider accounts, making expiry-awareness an absorbable feature.
Strong machine events and exact payment delta, but native Shopify per-fulfillment capture and a live split-fulfillment capture app materially weaken whitespace.
Balances and reset dates are clean, but Apollo waterfall enrichment and other multi-provider enrichment tools already perform the key routing decision.

new_search_rules: Do not treat multi-provider routing as whitespace merely because it lacks an expiry variable; if an incumbent already owns the routing decision, expiry-awareness is likely a feature rather than a business.
Prefer timing/allocation wedges that can operate from read-only quota state plus an existing queue, so the first version does not sit on the request path.
When a candidate relies on expiring credits, verify whether the adjacent category already has a router/orchestrator before spending time quantifying expiry leakage.

bank guarantee or standby-LC cash-margin release monitoring
unused corporate airline ticket value recovery
data-enrichment cross-provider credit routing as a standalone wedge
